ja: 兄は休日になるとほとんどの時間をキャンプ道具の手入れに使っているけど、実際にキャンプに行くことはめったにない。
en: My brother spends most of his days off maintaining his camping gear, but he rarely actually goes camping.
alternatives: My brother spends most of his days off taking care of his camping gear, but he hardly ever actually goes camping.
On his days off, my brother spends most of his time looking after his camping equipment, but he seldom actually goes camping.
point: gear も equipment も数えられない名詞なので s を付けない

ja: 姉が去年から通っているボルダリングジムのオーナーが、週末に初心者向けのクラスを始めたらしいよ。
en: The owner of the bouldering gym my sister has been going to since last year has apparently started a weekend class for beginners.
alternatives: Apparently the owner of the bouldering gym my sister's been going to since last year has started a beginners' class on weekends.
I heard the owner of the bouldering gym that my sister has been going to since last year has started a weekend class for beginners.
point: 主語は「オーナー」。長い修飾の後で動詞 has を忘れない

ja: 土曜日にロードバイクを点検してもらうつもりだったんだけど、行ってみたらその店がもうつぶれてたんだよね。
en: I was going to have my road bike serviced on Saturday, but it turned out the shop had already closed down.
alternatives: I was planning to get my road bike checked on Saturday, but when I went, the shop had already closed for good.
I meant to have my road bike looked at on Saturday, but it turned out the shop had already gone out of business.
point: 「点検してもらう」は have + 物 + 過去分詞

ja: 母は定年後に始めた水彩画にすっかりはまっていて、最近は地元の展示会にまで作品を出しているんです。
en: My mom has really gotten into the watercolor painting she took up after retiring, and she's even been entering her work in local exhibitions lately.
alternatives: My mother is totally hooked on the watercolor painting she took up after she retired, and lately she's even been submitting her work to local exhibitions.
My mom has gotten really into watercolors since she took them up after retiring, and recently she's even been showing her work at local exhibitions.
point: 「始める（趣味）」は take up、「はまる」は get into

ja: 昨日電話くれたとき、ちょうど庭でトマトを植えてたんだ。
en: I was planting tomatoes in the garden when you called yesterday.
alternatives: When you called yesterday, I was planting tomatoes in the garden.
I was in the garden planting tomatoes when you called yesterday.
point: 途中だった動作は過去進行形、割り込んだ出来事は過去形

ja: 今週末に本当にしたいのは、家でのんびり本を読むことなんだ。
en: What I really want to do this weekend is relax at home and read.
alternatives: What I really want to do this weekend is stay home and read a book.
All I really want to do this weekend is chill at home with a book.
point: 「〜したいこと」は What I want to do で主語にする

ja: ギターって、いつから習ってるの？
en: How long have you been learning the guitar?
alternatives: How long have you been taking guitar lessons?
When did you start learning the guitar?
point: 今も続いている期間は How long have you been 〜ing

ja: 差し支えなければ、休みの日は普段どう過ごされているのか、お聞きしたいなと思っていたんですが。
en: If you don't mind my asking, I was wondering how you usually spend your days off.
alternatives: I was wondering, if you don't mind me asking, how you normally spend your days off.
If it's not too personal, I was wondering what you usually do on your days off.
point: how 以下は疑問文の語順にせず how you usually spend

ja: 学生のころにピアノを続けていればよかったなあ。そうすれば今ごろ好きな曲が弾けたのに。
en: I wish I'd kept up the piano when I was a student. Then I could play my favorite songs now.
alternatives: If only I had kept playing the piano as a student. I'd be able to play my favorite songs now.
I wish I hadn't quit the piano as a student. I'd be able to play the songs I like now.
point: 過去の後悔は wish + had 過去分詞、今できたはずのことは could + 原形
